faq.q: Does looking up an IP send my data anywhere?
faq.a: Only on the Public IP Lookup tab, and only when you press the button. That sends a request from your browser directly to ipapi.co, a third-party geolocation service that processes it under its own privacy policy. The 'My Connection', WebRTC and IP Toolkit tabs run entirely in your browser and make no network requests at all.

faq.q: What can the offline IP Toolkit calculate?
faq.a: Everything runs locally: validate and classify IPv4/IPv6 addresses (private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, multicast, reserved), convert IPv4 to and from its 32-bit integer, a full CIDR/subnet calculator (network, broadcast, masks, first/last host, usable count), a 'is this IP inside this CIDR' check, and a subnet splitter. It correctly handles /31 as a point-to-point pair (RFC 3021) and /32 as a single host.

faq.q: Why does the Local IP (WebRTC) tab show a .local hostname instead of a real IP?
faq.a: Modern browsers deliberately mask your real local address behind an mDNS hostname ending in .local to prevent the well-known WebRTC privacy leak. Seeing .local (or no address at all) means your browser's privacy protection is working. Any detection happens inside your browser and isn't sent anywhere.

faq.q: How accurate is the geolocation, and can I save my results?
faq.a: IP geolocation from any service is typically accurate only to city/region level, and VPNs, proxies or mobile carriers can show a very different location — treat it as approximate. Private, loopback and link-local addresses can't be geolocated at all. You can download or copy a text report of your findings, and recent lookups are kept (up to 10) in your browser under ipl_hist so you can re-run one without retyping.
